knowledge:
- key_parameters: spacers=Character vector of short DNA spacer sequences to align ;; seeds=Character vector of short RNAi seed sequences to align ;; bsgenome=A BSgenome object corresponding to the reference genome used for extracting protospacer and PAM sequences ;; crisprNuclease=A CrisprNuclease object (from crisprBase) specifying the nuclease to constrain PAM search ;; n_mismatches=Integer specifying the maximum number of mismatches allowed between the query and target sequences ;; canonical=Logical indicating whether to restrict the search to canonical PAM sequences (TRUE) or allow non-canonical PAMs (FALSE) ;; bwa_index=Character string specifying the path prefix of the BWA index
- alternatives: addSpacerAlignments=A function in the crisprDesign package recommended for comprehensive gRNA design and off-target annotation within the broader crisprVerse ecosystem
- when_to_use: Use when you need to perform fast on-target and off-target searches for CRISPR gRNA spacer sequences across a genome for any CRISPR nuclease, or when mapping short RNAi (siRNA/shRNA) seed sequences to a reference genome to predict off-target effects.
- pitfalls: OS Compatibility=The package is supported on macOS and Linux only (not supported on Windows) ;; Index Requirement=Users must build a BWA index using Rbwa::bwa_build_index before running alignments, as standard FASTA files cannot be queried directly without indexing.

workflows.name: crispr_grna_alignment
workflows.intent: Align CRISPR gRNA spacer sequences to a reference genome to identify on-target and off-target sites with PAM constraints.
input: genome_fasta.fa (FASTA file of the reference genome)
spacers_vector (Character vector of gRNA spacer sequences)
workflows.stages: 1. Build a BWA index from the reference genome FASTA using Rbwa::bwa_build_index ;; 2. Load the corresponding BSgenome object and CrisprNuclease object ;; 3. Align spacers and annotate PAMs using runCrisprBwa
workflows.code:
library(Rbwa)
fasta <- system.file(package="crisprBwa", "example/chr12.fa")
outdir <- tempdir()
index <- file.path(outdir, "chr12")
Rbwa::bwa_build_index(fasta,
                      index_prefix=index)

library(crisprBwa)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
data(SpCas9, package="crisprBase")
crisprNuclease <- SpCas9
bsgenome <- BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38
spacers <- c("AGCTGTCCGTGGGGGTCCGC",
             "CCCCTGCTGCTGTGCCAGGC",
             "ACGAACTGTAAAAGGCTTGG",
             "ACGAACTGTAACAGGCTTGG",
             "AAGGCCCTCAGAGTAATTAC")
runCrisprBwa(spacers,
             bsgenome=bsgenome,
             crisprNuclease=crisprNuclease,
             n_mismatches=3,
             canonical=FALSE,
             bwa_index=index)

workflows.name: rnai_seed_alignment
workflows.intent: Map short RNAi (siRNA/shRNA) seed sequences to a reference genome to predict putative off-targets without PAM constraints.
input: genome_fasta.fa (FASTA file of the reference genome)
seeds_vector (Character vector of RNAi seed sequences)
workflows.stages: 1. Build a BWA index from the reference genome FASTA using Rbwa::bwa_build_index ;; 2. Align seed sequences using runBwa
workflows.code:
library(Rbwa)
fasta <- system.file(package="crisprBwa", "example/chr12.fa")
outdir <- tempdir()
index <- file.path(outdir, "chr12")
Rbwa::bwa_build_index(fasta,
                      index_prefix=index)

library(crisprBwa)
seeds <- c("GTAAGCGGAGTGT", "AACGGGGAGATTG")
runBwa(seeds,
       n_mismatches=2,
       bwa_index=index)
